title: Lay three reinforcing bars on the bolsters at 100 mm centres with 20 mm end cover
instruction: Lay the three rust-brown bars across the two grey bolsters, parallel and 10 cm apart centre to centre, with at least 2 cm between each bar end and the wooden side forms.
context: Reinforcing iron and rebar workers (O*NET 47-2171) place bars at the spacing and concrete cover the drawings call for, on bolsters or chairs that hold them at the right height in the slab, and the spacing and cover are checked with a tape before the concrete is poured: bars too far apart leave the slab weak between them, and a bar too close to the form ends up with too little concrete over it, so it rusts and the concrete spalls. The work is measured placement of long, awkward bars: each is taken from a stack, turned square to the supports and set down on its mark without disturbing the bars already laid. Here the bars are stacked on both sides of the slab, each side within reach of one arm.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Four kinds of thing, all plain rectangular blocks. (1) Slab forms: four fixed plywood boards, 10 mm thick and 25 mm tall, closing a rectangle whose inner faces are at x 10.0 and 42.0 cm and y -23.0 and +23.0 cm. The two side forms run along x (320 mm long) with their inner faces at y +23.0 and -23.0 cm; the front and back forms run along y (480 mm long) at x 9.0 to 10.0 cm and 42.0 to 43.0 cm. (2) Two bolsters: fixed grey plastic bar supports, 280 mm long along x (x 12.0 to 40.0 cm), 12 mm wide and 20 mm tall, centred at y +12.0 cm and y -12.0 cm inside the forms; their tops are 20 mm above the table. (3) Four racks: fixed weathered-timber blocks, 20 mm wide along x and 20 mm tall, at x 15.0 and 41.0 cm, outside the forms: two 140 mm long (along y) centred at y +34.0 cm on the left, two 80 mm long centred at y -32.0 cm on the right. (4) Three bars: loose stand-ins for 16 mm reinforcing bars, square aluminium tubes painted rust brown, 16 x 16 mm in section, 400 mm long, 1.6 mm wall, 0.10 kg each (a solid steel bar this size would weigh 0.80 kg), with flat faces. Each lies flat along x on its side's two racks (its underside 20 mm above the table), centred at x 28.0 cm, so it spans x 8.0 to 48.0 cm: two on the left at y +30.0 and +38.0 cm (64 mm apart edge to edge), one on the right at y -32.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table. A bar laid along y and centred on y 0 has 30 mm of cover at each end.
scoring: End state: the score is read from where the three bars lie at the last step. Each bar has four alike long faces: its 'tilt' is the angle between the vertical and the normal of whichever long face is nearest to facing up (any long face may be down: lying flat 0, rolled onto an edge 45, standing on an end 90), and its heading is the direction of its long side seen from above (either way round). A bar 'rests on' a bolster when, seen from above, its underside (its real, turned outline, not a bounding box) overlaps the bolster's top by at least 96 square mm (half of a square crossing of their 16 and 12 mm widths) and, at the centre of that overlap, its underside is within 3 mm of the bolster's top, above or below. A bar is 'on the bolsters' when it is tilted less than 5 degrees and rests on both, and 'laid' when it is also within 3 degrees of y. Its 'end cover' is the smaller of the two distances from its outline to the side forms' inner faces (y +23.0 and -23.0 cm). The 'mat' is the bars on the bolsters, in order along x. The 'spacing' of two laid bars next to each other in the mat is the distance along x between their centre lines where they cross each bolster's centre line (y +12.0 and -12.0 cm), as a tape laid along that bolster reads it; both readings count. A bar is 'on or across a form' when its outline seen from above overlaps a form board and its lowest point is at most 20 mm above the board's top. Score 0 if any bar ends off the table (its lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top), standing on an end or an edge (tilted more than 30 degrees), or on or across a form (it would stick out of the slab's edge). Otherwise: 1.0 if all three bars are laid with an end cover of 20 mm or more and both spacings are 100 mm +-5 mm at both bolsters; 0.75 if all three are laid with an end cover of 10 mm or more and both spacings are 100 mm +-12 mm at both bolsters, but not 1.0; 0.5 if two bars next to each other in the mat (no other bar on the bolsters between them) are both laid with an end cover of 20 mm or more and are 100 mm +-5 mm apart at both bolsters; 0.25 if at least one bar is laid with an end cover of 20 mm or more; 0 in every other case (no bar laid: bars along x, turned more than 3 degrees, on one bolster only, piled on each other). A bar left on its rack, or elsewhere on the table outside the forms, is simply not laid. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Any bar may go in any place, and the mat may lie anywhere along the bolsters. The trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with all three bars still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 3 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial, lay a tape along each bolster from the front form and read where each bar's centre line crosses it: the spacing is the difference of neighbouring readings, and a bar is within 3 degrees of y when its two readings (240 mm apart) differ by 12.6 mm or less. Read the end cover with a rule from each side form. A bar rests on a bolster when at least half its width is on the bolster and a 3 mm feeler gauge does not pass under it there.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The forms, bolsters and racks are fixed boxes; each bar is a plain uniform box of the stated size and mass (smooth, no ribs; a light tube stands in for a steel bar so the arms can carry it). Nothing is tied: a real mat is wire-tied where bars cross, here the bars only rest on the bolsters. The scorer sees only the bars, not the grippers, so a bar held still within 3 mm of both bolsters counts as resting on them.
reset_notes: Put each bar back on its side's two racks, lying flat along x and centred at x 28.0 cm: two on the left at y +30.0 and +38.0 cm, one on the right at y -32.0 cm. The forms, bolsters and racks are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
